themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Surge
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints spiked to 17 THIS WEEK, a 656% increase versus the 2.2-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks, suggesting either a sudden influx of unlicensed vendors or a coordinated enforcement gap in Upper East Side commercial corridors.
evidence: 17 mobile food vendor complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.2 weekly average (z-score: 6.05)
Statistically significant anomaly suggests new problem, not seasonal pattern
reporting_angles: Investigate whether vendors are concentrated in specific commercial zones (Madison Ave, Lexington Ave, etc.) or scattered across the district
Interview Department of Health and Mental Hygiene about recent enforcement activity and whether vendor licensing renewals or street-vending permits changed recently

themes_detail.label: Street Noise Intensifying
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints jumped 133% LAST WEEK to 46 complaints versus a 19.8-complaint weekly average, signaling a sharp deterioration in sound conditions across public spaces.
evidence: 46 street/sidewalk noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 19.8 weekly average (z-score: 5.18)
Complements long-running noise trend (1,570 total noise complaints over 90 days) with new acceleration
reporting_angles: Identify geographic hotspots: are complaints concentrated near construction sites, transit hubs (86th St Lexington station), or nightlife venues?
Canvass residents along high-complaint blocks to characterize the noise source (construction, street performers, sirens, bars) and timing

themes_detail.label: Litter Basket Shortage
themes_detail.summary: Litter basket requests exploded to 10 complaints LAST WEEK, a 627% spike versus the 1.4-complaint weekly average, indicating residents are signaling inadequate street-level waste infrastructure.
evidence: 10 litter basket request complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly average (z-score: 17.82, highest z-score in dataset)
Convergence with dumpster (967% spike) and commercial disposal complaints (700% spike) suggests broader waste management crisis
reporting_angles: Map which blocks or neighborhoods are filing litter basket requests to identify underserved areas
Request Sanitation Department data on basket inventory and maintenance schedules to see if service cuts or removals coincide with this week

themes_detail.label: Commercial Waste Disposal Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dumpster complaints (967% spike to 4 LAST WEEK) and commercial disposal complaints (700% spike to 5 LAST WEEK) are converging, suggesting a district-wide commercial waste management breakdown affecting restaurants, retailers, and offices.
evidence: Dumpster complaints: 4 LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 7.49)
Commercial disposal complaints: 5 LAST WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average (z-score: 6.29)
Combined signal across two complaint types indicates systemic issue, not isolated incidents
reporting_angles: Interview commercial tenants (restaurants, grocery stores, offices) about waste pickup delays, overflow dumpsters, or missed collection days
Contact commercial waste haulers serving the Upper East Side to determine if labor shortages, truck breakdowns, or routing changes caused the collapse in service

themes_detail.label: Tree Canopy Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints spiked 900% TWO WEEKS AGO to 5 complaints versus a 0.5-complaint weekly average, suggesting environmental stress or deferred maintenance across the district's street tree inventory.
evidence: 5 dead/dying tree complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 6.36)
Aligns with long-standing community board budget request for street tree care and repairs
reporting_angles: Obtain Parks Department street tree inventory and maintenance records to identify which blocks have sick or neglected trees
Interview Parks maintenance staff about staffing constraints, pest infestations (scale, beetle, fungus), or drought stress affecting the district
